Container.Name: Obelisk
Container.Overview:
One container to run and manage an ARK: Survival Ascended cluster. Pick your maps and Obelisk builds the rest - generating the compose, assigning ports, keeping one shared settings file across every map, relaying chat between them and to Discord, and giving you a status page and admin controls in the browser.
Only the fields below are needed to start: two folders, the socket and a port. They hold different things - settings in one, the big game files in the other - so read the descriptions before picking where each goes. Everything else - maps, mods, rates, Discord, wipe schedules, time zone - is set in the web UI once it is running. After starting, check the container log for a one-time setup code, then open the WebUI.

Config.Name: Obelisk data
Config.Description: Obelisk's own settings: the cluster definition, your map selection, the mod ID list and its order, ports and RAM, admin credentials and backup snapshots. No game files and no saves live here - it stays small (kilobytes), and ordinary array storage is fine. This is the half that cannot be downloaded again, so all of it is backed up.

Config.Name: Ark data
Config.Description: The large ARK files: the server install, the MODS it downloads, and the world SAVES, plus the shared config and the cross-map transfer data. Tens of gigabytes - put this on an SSD, NVMe or ZFS pool, NOT the spinning array, because ASA is very I/O hungry. Backups take the saves and transfer data from here and deliberately skip the server install and the mods: those are re-downloaded from the mod IDs kept in Obelisk data, so there is no reason to carry them off the machine.

Config.Name: Docker socket
Config.Description: Lets Obelisk create and manage the map containers.

Config.Name: WebUI port
Config.Description: Status page and admin UI. Change the host side here and Obelisk follows it - there is no second port to keep in sync.
